title: Go-Live Sentinel: Quick Ops Reference and Release Notes (Oct 2024)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational-first reference for the upcoming go-live window. It combines the preflight checklist we run at T-72 to T-0, an abbreviated hourly calendar for the first 12 hours after cutover, and a concise release-notes draft to push to product and CS. This doc is deliberately brief so SRE/Release leads can print or paste into the oncall console.

Scope & constraints:
- Applies to API surface: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings for hosted clusters in us-west1 and eu-west1 only.
- Does NOT cover Dedicated hardware migrations or Private deployments (separate runbooks).
- Cutover window: 2024-10-31 00:00 UTC — primary region us-west1 first, eu-west1 staggered +15m.

Owners & contacts (primary):
- Release lead: Asha Patel (pager: asha.patel@redwood.com, slack: #release-ops)
- SRE lead: Daniel Park (pager: dpark-sre)
- Infra oncall: Evelyn Brooks (rotation: week of 2024-10-28)
- Product comms: Sofia Ramirez (for release notes/channel posts)
- Exec notify: Oliver Nguyen (for escalations > 30m)

Preflight checklist (T-72, T-24, T-6):
- T-72: Finalize migration manifest + model pins (confirm model SHA and quantization profile). Attach to JIRA-4521.
- T-72: Verify canary job passes (1000 synthetic requests across endpoints, p95 latency < configured SLO).
- T-24: Run long-tail smoke (48-hour tail simulation) and upload results (s3://ops-artifacts/release-2024-10-31/).
- T-24: Capacity reserve set (10% buffer) and burst policy validated in staging.
- T-6: Confirm rollout policy: phased by region, fallback to smaller model variant if OOMs.
- T-6: Communication draft queued in #release-channel and product comms has scheduled post.
- T-1: Verify dashboard widgets: token-rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, kv-cache hit-rate, GPU mem headroom.
- T-0: All participants on call, list of blocked tickets is zero, final permission given by Release lead.

Immediate cutover checklist (T-0 to T+60m):
- T-0: Disable non-critical background jobs that write to inference metadata stores (reduce noise).
- +2m: Sanity smoke (20 req/min for 5m) to root endpoint; manual verify success rate >= 99.5%.
- +5m: Canary users (1% traffic) routed to new revision; monitor for errors and latency.
- +10m: Increase to 20% if canary stable; otherwise rollback to previous model. Criteria: error-rate delta > 1% absolute OR p95 increased > 40% -> rollback.
- +30m: Full traffic ramp decision checkpoint. If steady, flip remaining 80% in two steps at +5m increments.
- +60m: Final stabilization check: error rate, quota saturation, db write latency.

12-hour post-cutover calendar (high-level):
- Hour 1: Live watch (synchronous) — release lead, SRE, infra, product comms. Short check-ins at 0m, +15m, +30m, +60m.
- Hours 2-4: Reduced cadence checks every 60m. Focus: error groups, increased tail latency, KV cache saturation.
- Hours 4-12: Twice-daily check-ins (every 3 hours) with expanded roster including solutions-eng and CS for customer impact triage.
- Day 1 EOB: Post-launch triage meeting and preliminary rollforward items logged.

Minimum telemetry & dashboards to watch (links are in linked_artifacts):
- Token ingestion rate by route (alerts: sustained drop > 15% or spike > 200%).
- Model OOM counter (alert: any OOM during ramp).
- Error-class heatmap (5-minute resolution).
- KV cache hit-rate and miss growth (if miss-rate increases > 10% relative baseline, consider caching config rollback).

Critical failure modes & immediate actions (oddcase appendix):
- Catastrophic model OOMs across nodes: immediate action: activate fallback-model-route to 'quantized-small-v2', scale remaining capacity by +25% and open 'incident-critical' bridge. Notify execs.
- Control-plane write failure: switch to read-only mode for inference metadata; disable new deployments; run metadata-forwarder in safe mode.
- Region-wide networking issue (packet loss > 5%): fail traffic to eu-west1 standby region. If global, enable degraded mode response (rate-limit at API-gateway).

Rollback criteria (fast-path):
- Any sustained 5-minute error-rate > 3% absolute increase from baseline.
- Sustained p95 latency increase > 200ms absolute AND > 40% relative.
- Any data-loss or incorrect model outputs observed that materially affect downstream safety checks.
Procedure: revert traffic to previous model revision (automated by rollout controller), run smoke validation, re-assess in 15 minutes.

Smoke tests (runnable checklist):
- Auth check: token validation + refresh scenario (5 users).
- Small prompt: 10 short requests, ensure responses contain expected marker tokens.
- Long prompt: 5 long sequences, verify kv-cache doesn't grow unbounded.
- Embedding sanity: cosine similarity checks vs golden vectors (>0.92).
- Throughput burst: 200 rps for 30s, observe p95 and CPU/GPU throttling.

Release notes (draft to product & cs):
Title: Performance & stability rollout — model revision oct-31
Summary: We’re rolling a model revision that improves long-context memory handling and reduces median token cost for chat by ~8%. This launch is focused on hosted API in us-west1 and eu-west1.
What changed: Updated model binary to model-rev-2024-10-18 (quantize profile Q3), tuned KV-cache retention to reduce recompute.
Why it matters: Users should see fewer context truncations on long chats and slightly lower unit cost on chat workloads.
Known issues: In early canaries some large-batch workloads observed p99 increases; we’ve added throttling to mitigate — contact support if you see persistent tail latency.
Rollout plan: Gradual regional ramp with automated rollback criteria; we’ll monitor for 12 hours post-cutover and post a status summary.
Contact & next steps: For customer-facing questions, CS will direct to #cs-release and open tickets with label release-oct-2024.

Post-launch follow-ups (log for 72h):
- Capture sample traces for any request with latency > 99th percentile.
- Run regression evals on the golden prompt set (script: infra/tools/regression_eval.sh) and attach to JIRA-4521.
- Economics: compute tokens/sec and per-token cost delta for first 24 hours and report to finance by EOD+1.

Notes and unresolved questions:
- Need confirmation from infra on burst NIC limits for us-west1 — ticket created in JIRA-4580.
- Confirm SLO page update cadence (who will publish: product comms).

Appendix: Quick comms snippets (copy-paste)
- #release-channel short status (at +15m): "Canary at 20% stable — p95 within expected range, no error spike. Proceeding with ramp."
- Customer banner (CS template): "We’re deploying a small performance upgrade to our hosted API on Oct 31. Expect no action required; reach out to support if you experience latency or accuracy regressions."

End of doc. Keep this page as the primary oncall reference for the Oct 31 go-live window. Archive subsequent notes to the linked Confluence index and attach any postmortem items to JIRA-4521.
